originalTitle: US stocks today: Nasdaq rallies to sharply higher close; chip surge offsets Iran worries
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a good day, with the Nasdaq ending significantly higher. This was largely due to companies that make computer chips, such as Micron, doing well because of a big investment plan related to artificial intelligence. Even though there are concerns about tensions between the US and Iran, the market still went up. The fact that jobless claims remained stable also helped, showing that the labor market is still strong. This positive trend is a good sign as investors look ahead to companies releasing their earnings reports and evaluating their values.

originalTitle: Groww responds to Nithin Kamath tweet: Direct mutual funds remain free for DIY investors
simplifiedContent: Groww, an investment platform, has confirmed that it will continue to offer direct mutual funds for free to individual investors who manage their own investments. This means that people who use Groww to buy and sell mutual funds on their own won't have to pay any extra fees. Groww made this announcement after some recent discussions about mutual funds in the market had raised questions about their policies. This is important because it gives investors clarity on what to expect from Groww and helps them make informed decisions about their investments. Overall, Groww's decision to keep direct mutual funds free is good news for individual investors who use their platform.

originalTitle: Sebi cancels registration of 12 research analysts over unpaid renewal fees
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market regulator, Sebi, has cancelled the registration of 12 research analysts because they didn't pay their renewal fees. This means that these analysts can no longer legally provide research and recommendations to investors. Sebi took this action after sending notices to the analysts and not getting any response. The analysts' failure to pay their fees and respond to Sebi's notices led to the cancellation of their registrations. This matters because it helps Sebi maintain standards and ensure that only qualified and responsible analysts are providing investment advice to the public.

originalTitle: HDFC Bank Q1 results date: Private lender to announce June quarter earnings on 18 July
simplifiedContent: HDFC Bank, a private bank, will announce its earnings for the quarter ending June on July 18. This means the bank will share how it performed financially during the months of April, May, and June. The bank's Board of Directors will meet on July 18 to review and approve the financial results before making them public. This is important because it will give investors an idea of how the bank is doing and help them decide if they want to invest in it. By announcing its earnings, HDFC Bank is following standard practice to keep its investors informed about its financial performance.

originalTitle: Russia's largest private lender Alfa Bank tests crypto trading, plans suite of crypto services ahead of govt legislation
simplifiedContent: Alfa Bank, a large bank in Russia, is trying out a new feature that lets people trade cryptocurrencies, like Bitcoin, through its investment app. The bank plans to offer more services related to cryptocurrencies in the future. This is happening before the Russian government puts out official rules and laws about digital assets like cryptocurrencies. This matters because it shows that a major bank is getting ready to work with cryptocurrencies, which could make it easier for people to use them. It's a sign that the bank is preparing for potential changes in the law that will affect how people can buy, sell, and use cryptocurrencies.

originalTitle: Multibagger defence stock Apollo Micro Systems to be in focus on Friday; here's why
simplifiedContent: A company called Apollo Micro Systems is making a big move by buying a large part of another company called Premier Explosives. Apollo Micro Systems is spending ₹1,550 crore to buy 41.33% of Premier Explosives, which could help India's defense industry. This deal might get a lot of attention on Friday because it's a significant move for Apollo Micro Systems. The company plans to finish the deal by December 2026 and might even buy more shares as part of the agreement. This matters because it could potentially impact the value of Apollo Micro Systems' stock.
